entities.summary:
Hyundai Motor Company, founded in Seoul in 1967 by Chung Ju-yung and now part of the Hyundai Motor Group (with Kia and Genesis), is South Korea's largest automaker and the world's third-largest automotive group by sales volume — producing 7.2 million vehicles annually, employing 250,000 people, and transforming South Korea's economic development through vertical integration of steel, shipping, and automotive production in one family conglomerate. Hyundai's rise from a 1967 startup to a global top-3 automaker in 55 years is among history's most dramatic industrial ascents.

Chung Ju-yung (founder of Hyundai Engineering and Construction, 1947) applied his construction conglomerate's vertical integration model to automobiles — building the Ulsan automotive complex (1968, Korea's first dedicated car plant), and initially assembling Ford Cortinas under license. The first Hyundai-designed car, the Pony (1975, designed by Giorgio Giugiaro), was the first Korean-designed automobile and was exported to Canada in 1984 — beginning Hyundai's international expansion.

Hyundai's quality transformation (2000-2010) — from being North America's lowest-rated automaker (1990s) to among the highest (2010s) — is one of the most remarkable brand rehabilitation stories in automotive history. The 10-year/100,000-mile warranty (introduced 1998) forced quality improvement. Hyundai's IONIQ 5 and Genesis G90 demonstrate Korean automotive leadership in EV design. The Hyundai-Kia Group's 2023 acquisition of Boston Dynamics (robotics) signals diversification from automotive into robotics and future mobility.
